title: Mapp v. Ohio
principle: Exclusionary rule - evidence obtained illegally is inadmissible
facts: Police entered home without warrant and seized contraband
holding: Evidence obtained via illegal search is inadmissible in court

title: Terry v. Ohio
principle: Stop and frisk - reasonable suspicion standard
facts: Police stopped suspect based on reasonable suspicion and conducted pat-down
holding: Stop-and-frisk allowed under reasonable suspicion

title: Miranda v. Arizona
principle: Right to counsel - custodial interrogation rights
facts: Defendant confessed during custodial interrogation without warnings
holding: Custodial statements require Miranda warnings

title: Chimel v. California
facts: Warrantless search of home incident to arrest
holding: Search incident to arrest limited to immediate area

title: United States v. Ross
facts: Police searched vehicle based on probable cause
holding: Vehicle searchable upon probable cause without warrant

title: Payton v. New York
facts: Police entered home without warrant to arrest
holding: Warrant required for arrest in private residence

title: Florida v. Jardines
facts: Police walked dog on porch during sniff
holding: Front porch is protected curtilage, not open area

title: Hudson v. Michigan
holding: Knock and announce may be excused under certain conditions

title: Wong Sun v. United States
holding: Taint may dissipate if attenuated from illegality

title: Whren v. United States
holding: Any traffic violation justifies stop

title: Carroll v. United States
facts: Warrantless vehicle search with probable cause
holding: Vehicle searchable without warrant

title: Katz v. United States
holding: Fourth Amendment protects reasonable expectation of privacy

title: Goldman v. United States
facts: Government used pen register without warrant
holding: No privacy expectation in information voluntarily revealed to third parties

title: Oliver v. United States
facts: Police entered private farm without warrant
holding: No Fourth Amendment protection for open fields

title: United States v. Karo
facts: Government used pen register with subpoena
holding: Pen registers not covered by Fourth Amendment

title: United States v. White
facts: Government used informant with hidden transmitter
holding: No expectation of privacy when speaking to government informant

title: Florida v. Riley
holding: No privacy expectation in backyard visible from aircraft

title: California v. Green
holding: Prior testimony admissible if witness unavailable

title: Ohio v. Roberts
facts: Used prior testimony when witness absent
holding: Prior testimony OK if unavailable and had opportunity to cross-examine

title: Crawford v. Washington
facts: State used taped statement without testimony
holding: Testimonial out-of-court statements barred unless witness unavailable

title: Melendez-Diaz v. Massachusetts
facts: Used lab certifications without analyst testimony
holding: Analyst must testify if defendant requests

title: Williams v. Illinois
holding: Lab reports as business records admissible

title: Gideon v. Wainwright
holding: Counsel required for felony defendants

title: Argersinger v. Hamlin
holding: No imprisonment without counsel

title: Alabama v. Scotland
facts: Defendant convicted of petty offense without counsel
holding: No counsel required for petty offenses

title: United States v. Wade
holding: Counsel required for lineup

title: Kirby v. Illinois
facts: Police conducted showup immediately after crime
holding: No counsel required for showup

title: Manson v. Brathwaite
holding: Identification admissible if reliable despite suggestiveness

title: Neil v. Biggers
holding: Totality of circumstances test for identification

title: Schneckloth v. Bustamonte
facts: Police asked to search car, defendant consented
holding: Consent valid if voluntary

title: United States v. Mathews
holding: One occupant can consent to common areas

title: Georgia v. Randolph
holding: Objection makes search invalid

title: Fernandez v. California
facts: One occupant consented while other arrested outside
holding: Absent occupant consent valid

title: United States v. Moncera
holding: Probable cause for vehicle search from odor

title: California v. Acevedo
holding: Can search container without warrant if probable cause

title: California v. Beheler
holding: Brief detention allowed for ID

title: United States v. Clemente
holding: Warrantless entry allowed for emergencies

title: Brigham v. Stuart
holding: Hot pursuit allows warrantless entry

title: Michigan v. Summers
holding: Can detaining occupant during lawful search

title: Florida v. B. Smith
holding: Search incident to arrest - person and area within control

title: United States v. Hensley
holding: Investigative stop based on flyer valid

title: Devenport v. Hayes
holding: Profile alone insufficient for stop

title: Navarette v. California
holding: 911 call provides reasonable suspicion

title: Wardlow v. Illinois
holding: Unprovoked flight creates reasonable suspicion

title: Illinois v. Wardlow
facts: Suspect in high crime area fled
holding: Flight + area creates reasonable suspicion

title: United States v. Sokolov
holding: Dog alert provides probable cause

title: United States v. Place
holding: Dog sniff not search if no intrusion

title: Jardines v. Florida
holding: Porch is curtilage - not open area

title: United States v. Wilson
holding: Inventory search allowed for safety

title: Colorado v. Connelly
holding: Coerced confessions barred - must be voluntary

title: Yarborough v. Alvarado
facts: Was suspect in custody for Miranda
holding: Objective test for custody - reasonable person standard

title: Howes v. Fields
holding: Prison interrogation not automatically custodial

title: Maryland v. Shatzer
holding: 14-day break breaks interrogation chain
